evidence.snippet: Clopidogrel is an antithrombotic prodrug, whose active metabolite inhibits platelet function by irreversibly binding to the platelet receptor for adenosine diphosphate, P2Y(12).
evidence.explanation: Establishes that clopidogrel is a prodrug that generates an active metabolite responsible for its antiplatelet effect.

evidence.snippet: Clopidogrel is a thienopyridine that selectively and irreversibly inhibits the ADP purinergic receptor P2Y12 and the subsequent ADP-mediated platelet activation.
evidence.explanation: Directly states clopidogrel (via its active metabolite) irreversibly inhibits the P2Y12 receptor.

evidence.snippet: Adenosine diphosphate (ADP) is the major platelet agonist, which is important in the shape changes, stability, and growth of the thrombus.
evidence.explanation: P2Y12 is an ADP receptor; ADP acting through P2Y12 positively regulates platelet aggregation. The pharmacologic blockade of P2Y12 reduces platelet aggregation (per the same paper).

paper.title: Inhibitory Effect of Flavonolignans on the P2Y12 Pathway in Blood Platelets.

evidence.snippet: Clopidogrel is a thienopyridine that selectively and irreversibly inhibits the ADP purinergic receptor P2Y12 and the subsequent ADP-mediated platelet activation.
evidence.explanation: Shows that P2Y12 mediates ADP-driven platelet activation, supporting that P2Y12 positively regulates platelet aggregation.

paper.title: Clopidogrel generic formulations in the era of new antiplatelets: a systematic review.

evidence.snippet: Platelet activation and aggregation play a seminal role in the arterial thrombus formation that precipitates acute manifestations of atherothrombotic disease.
evidence.explanation: Establishes platelet aggregation as contributing to arterial thrombus formation, which causes ischemic stroke (an atherothrombotic disease manifestation).

paper.title: Oral antiplatelet therapy for atherothrombotic disease: overview of current and emerging treatment options.

evidence.snippet: An abundance of evidence supports aspirin and clopidogrel use for secondary stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: Clinical evidence that antiplatelet therapy (clopidogrel) prevents stroke, implicating platelet aggregation in stroke pathogenesis.
